doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Playback of 'As Time Goes By'
summary: Rowe plays 'As Time Goes By' from the CD and points out a modulation in the last A section that Person does not recall.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I want to see if I can find this particular tune that I just loved the beginning of, that has the Houston Person sound down. Let me see if I’ve got it. I don’t got it. There it is.
A Houston Person sound, oh. Let me hear this so I can learn it.
[audio interlude: “As Time Goes By” from the CD “Why Not”]
That is romantic as all get out.
I get a lot of calls about that song.
Now you did something at the end of this tune too, do you recall? The last A [section]?
No you don’t? Let me see if I can find it. I hope I don’t make a liar out of myself. It must have been right at the end, you did this very cool modulation, right at the end of that tune.
Yeah, you’re going to have to listen to yourself now, because it was neat, believe me.
You took the last A and you went like, I don’t know, it was nice, real nice.
Okay, okay. Gee. Yeah, I’ve got to listen to that.
